content.motivation: The changes refactor the `ChatOptions` and related builder pattern implementations to improve code organization, maintainability, and consistency across different option types (ChatOptions, ToolCallingChatOptions, StructuredOutputChatOptions). Key changes include introducing a `mutate()` method for easier copying, enhancing the builder pattern with generics for type safety, and consolidating common builder logic into a base class.
goodPoints: Introduction of the `mutate()` method in `ChatOptions` and `DefaultChatOptions` provides a standardized way to create a builder from existing options, promoting immutability and easier cloning.
The `Builder` interface and its implementations now use generics (`<B extends Builder<B>>`) for better type safety and fluent chaining, reducing the need for explicit casting.
Consolidation of common builder logic for `ChatOptions` into `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder` and extending it in `DefaultToolCallingChatOptions.Builder` reduces code duplication.
The new `AbstractChatOptionsTests` provides a solid foundation for testing various `ChatOptions` implementations, ensuring consistent testing practices.
Nullable annotations are consistently applied to builder methods and fields, improving code clarity and safety.
badPoints: The `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder` contains commented-out code (`// TODO remove`, `/* TODO move builder as an inner class */`) which should be cleaned up.
The `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder`'s `combineWith` method is not fully generic and accepts `ChatOptions.Builder<?>` which could lead to runtime issues if the `other` builder is not compatible.
The `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder.build()` method includes a `// TODO: Assert.notNull() as required` comment, indicating potential missing validation.
The `StructuredOutputChatOptions.Builder` interface is missing the `@FunctionalInterface` annotation, although PMD flags it, it's a good practice for single-abstract-method interfaces.
content.suggestion: 1. Clean up commented-out code in `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder`. 2. Make the `combineWith` method in `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder` more robust or add specific checks for expected builder types. 3. Implement the `Assert.notNull()` checks in `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder.build()`. 4. Add `@FunctionalInterface` to `StructuredOutputChatOptions.Builder`.

details: Introduced `mutate()` default method to create a builder from existing options.
Modified `ChatOptions.Builder` to use generics `<B extends Builder<B>>` for type-safe chaining.
Added `combineWith(ChatOptions.Builder<?> other)` method to the `Builder` interface.
Updated `ChatOptions.builder()` factory method to return `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder`.
Implemented `mutate()` to return a new `ChatOptions.Builder` initialized with current option values.
Added a private constructor for creating `DefaultChatOptions` directly from builder values.
Implemented `equals()` and `hashCode()` for proper comparison of `DefaultChatOptions` objects.
The `copy()` method now delegates to `mutate().build()`.
Refactored to use generic type `<B extends DefaultChatOptionsBuilder<B>>` for self-referencing return types.
Builder fields (`model`, `frequencyPenalty`, etc.) are now protected members instead of being held within a `DefaultChatOptions` instance.
The `build()` method now constructs a new `DefaultChatOptions` object using its private constructor.
The `combineWith()` method has been updated to merge properties from another `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder`.
Added a `self()` helper method to return the correctly typed builder instance.
Modified `ToolCallingChatOptions.Builder` to extend `ChatOptions.Builder<B>` and use generics `<B extends Builder<B>>`.
Updated builder methods (`toolCallbacks`, `toolNames`, etc.) to return the generic type `B`.
The static `builder()` method now returns `DefaultToolCallingChatOptions.Builder<>`.
The `Builder` class now extends `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder` to inherit common options.
Added specific fields for tool-related options (`toolCallbacks`, `toolNames`, `toolContext`, `internalToolExecutionEnabled`).
The `build()` method now creates a `DefaultToolCallingChatOptions` and sets both common and tool-specific options.
The `copy()` method is updated to use `mutate().build()`.
The `mutate()` method is implemented to return a `DefaultToolCallingChatOptions.Builder` initialized with current values.
The `Builder` class is now a nested static class instead of a top-level class.
Added a generic `Builder` interface with an `outputSchema` method.
Introduced an abstract test class for testing `ChatOptions` implementations.
Includes tests for `builderShouldReturnNewInstances` and `testMutateBehavior`.
Requires subclasses to implement `getConcreteOptionsClass()` and `readyToBuildBuilder()`.

issues.title: Commented-out code in DefaultChatOptionsBuilder
issues.detail: The file contains commented-out code blocks like '// TODO remove' and '/* TODO move builder as an inner class */'. This code should be removed or addressed.

issues.title: Potentially unsafe combineWith method signature
issues.detail: The `combineWith` method accepts `ChatOptions.Builder<?>`. If the provided builder is not a `DefaultChatOptionsBuilder` or a compatible subclass, the internal casting or property access could fail at runtime.

issues.title: Missing validation in DefaultChatOptionsBuilder.build()
issues.detail: The `build()` method has a TODO comment indicating that `Assert.notNull()` checks might be required for certain fields. These validations should be implemented to ensure the created options object is in a valid state.

issues.title: Missing @FunctionalInterface annotation
issues.detail: The `Builder` interface within `StructuredOutputChatOptions` has only one abstract method and should be annotated with `@FunctionalInterface` for clarity and to adhere to common Java practices. PMD also flags this.
